intro: The income tax rates for Australian residents, the income thresholds where each rate starts, and what the rates leave out, including the Medicare levy.
explanation:
## Each rate applies only to the income inside its band

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) tables give each band's tax as a fixed amount plus a number of cents for every dollar above the band's starting point. That structure shows how the bands work. A rate applies only to the part of your **taxable income** that sits inside its band, and crossing into a higher band does not raise the tax on the income below it. Taxable income is your assessable income less allowable deductions, so deductions come off before any rate is applied.

## These rates are for full-year residents with the full tax-free threshold

These rates suit someone who was a tax resident of Australia for the entire year and who qualifies for the whole {fact:au_tax_free_threshold} tax-free threshold. Part-year residents receive only a part-year threshold, and non-residents cannot claim the threshold at all. The [tax-free threshold](/au/tax/income-tax/tax-free-threshold/) page covers those cases.

## The Medicare levy and its surcharge are separate from these rates

Your taxable income also attracts the Medicare levy, which is {fact:au_medicare_levy_rate} and is not part of these rates. A surcharge that applies to some people is outside them too. A reduction or exemption from the levy is possible and turns on your income, your spouse's income and your situation. The surcharge is not automatic either: it depends on your personal circumstances. The [Medicare levy](/au/tax/income-tax/medicare-levy/) page covers the levy and how it differs from the surcharge.
